role: Regional authority responsible for expressway construction
stance_basis: described as cooperating with the project and providing technical data, with no opposition or advocacy expressed
summary: The Richmond Metropolitan Authority (RMA) is referenced throughout the document as the agency responsible for designing and constructing the Downtown Expressway, which forms the northern boundary of the Randolph Urban Renewal Area. RMA is described as cooperating with the Randolph Project, supplying roadway gradient data for noise studies, and proposing infrastructure improvements including bridges and a storm sewer relief line. The document notes two recommended changes to RMA's traffic proposals for the neighborhood, but RMA itself does not express any complaint or opposition.
complaint_summary: The Richmond Metropolitan Authority is described as proposing six bridges (five per the Randolph Plan) at various street crossings as part of the Downtown Expressway design through the project area.
summary_quote: A 48" diameter relief storm sewer is proposed by the Richmond Metropolitan Authority (RMA) from near the intersection of Lakeview and Shields Avenues to Swan Lake due to inadequate capacity of the existing 66" diameter conduit.

mentions.quote: Proposed roadway gradients were supplied by Richmond Metropolitan Authority.
other official agencies such as the State Water Control Board and Richmond Metropolitan Authority are cooperating to make the project successful.
